newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena reaches agreement with unions.
newsitem.headline: Sabena reaches agreement with unions.

text.p: Belgian national airline Sabena SA said on Monday it had reached initial agreement with trade unions on a range of measures aimed at bringing the company back into profit from 1998.
It said in a statement measures agreed on Monday, but not yet formally signed, include early retirement at 52, voluntary redundancies, part-time work, holidays without pay and internal transfers.

"I am very pleased with the consensus found with the trade unions. It is an important first step in ensuring the company's and its staff's future in a very competitive and difficult environment," said Sabena chief executive Paul Reutlinger.
Sabena said the measures agreed on Monday would be formally signed by all parties "in the next few days".
It said the company and trade unions were continuing negotiations about more flexible work conditions, and hoped these could be concluded by 31 October, 1996 at the latest.
Reutlinger said in June that Sabena needed to make extra savings of 4.7 billion francs, including 2 billion francs in labour-related cost reductions between now and 1998.
Swissair owns 49.5 percent of Sabena, with the rest held by the Belgian state.
